title: Cobalt Windfields
subtitle: A visual catalogue of the current environment
sourceNotes: Descriptions were checked against the active world and its source modules. Old compatibility names are not treated as visible scene contents.
World views show the current local working tree, including denser planting, expanded geology and the latest white clouds with a faint yellow tint.
The standard world uses seed 412 and a planet radius of approximately 128 metres. Placement and visible populations change with seed, growth, camera distance and clearance.

Studio plates use the source geometry and production material fragments under fixed lighting. They omit aerial haze, live articulation, growth deformation and post-processing; specimens are fitted individually rather than shown at a common scale.
Wildlife consists of eleven authored local animals near the settlement and wind corridor. These are ambient creatures, not a planet-wide population simulation.
Pip, Juniper and Marlo are local animated residents. Their names may be changed in the browser. Saved finds and garden content use the example gallery unless a backend is explicitly connected.
The construction notes predate some Windows additions. Current geometry and placement code take precedence over older prototype counts in those notes.

sections.title: Ground and landform
sections.intro: Warm, dry sand ties the blue geology and pale vegetation together. Broad relief remains readable from orbit; fine ripples and grains emerge at ground level.

items.name: Peach sand
items.description: Matte rose and peach washes pass across the ground, with lighter dune crests and cool muted shading in the hollows.

items.name: Wind ripples and grains
items.description: Irregular wind-laid ridges break into patches. Fine grains appear nearby and fade with distance, keeping the planet surface calm when viewed from above.

items.name: Sand banks and corridor
items.description: Broad cross-wind banks and dune shoulders frame a lower passage through the authored opening, with gentle continuous slopes around the settlement.

items.name: Settlement plateau
items.description: A dry, flattened clearing supports the shelter and its paths. The terrace, lookout and steps keep clear walking and sitting areas for the residents.

sections.title: Shelter and everyday objects
sections.intro: The home is built into cobalt bedrock, using rough stone, timber and suspended cloth. Its small domestic objects establish the scale of the landscape.

items.name: Slate shelter
items.description: Chipped stone walls and three heavy bedding slabs form a low refuge. Uneven roof shoulders, recessed timberwork and exposed rock edges soften its outline.

items.name: Canvas porch
items.description: A coral-brown woven awning hangs in a shallow curve above the terrace. Rope hems and slender supports define the cloth's edge.

items.name: Dry lookout and steps
items.description: A weathered stone ledge extends beside the shelter, with a low timber guard and three steps linking the supported deck to the sand.

items.name: Door and slatted screen
items.description: A timber door and open slatted screen sit inside the dark entrance, behind the clear porch route.

items.name: Timber windbreak
items.description: Uneven vertical slats form a permeable screen along the exposed flank of the home.

items.name: Bench and chair
items.description: A simple timber bench and a slightly turned chair provide resting places on the terrace and lookout.

items.name: Hanging lantern
items.description: One small warm lantern hangs beside the entrance, adding a restrained golden accent to the blue stone.

items.name: Porch stove and soup pot
items.description: A small iron stove stands on short legs, with a warm fire window, narrow pipe and soup pot. Muse uses a ladle when cooking.
items.source: life/museProps.ts: MuseProps; life/museRoam.ts: STOVE, cook routine

sections.title: Wildlife
sections.intro: Three local species share the stone corridor and sheltered planting. All are displayed at three times their authored size so their silhouettes remain readable in the landscape.

items.name: Sailback
items.description: Three cobalt-plated quadrupeds carry two ivory back sails, padded feet and a tapered tail. They walk among the Wind Ribs, open their sails, skim briefly and fold them again.

items.name: Kitelet
items.description: Five tiny ivory-bodied flyers have four coral diamond wings. They flutter and glide over the Seed Flats, then settle on the cupped leaves of their perches.

items.name: Sand Stitcher
items.description: Three small four-footed animals wear paired curved blue shell panels above peach faces. Each carries one straight dry stem, lowers it into a lee pocket and returns through the coral.

sections.title: Perches and gathered stems
sections.intro: The animals have physical places to land and leave material. These small structures connect their movement to the surrounding vegetation and sand.

items.name: Seed-cup perch A
items.description: A broad ivory cup rises on a crooked stem, with a strong midrib and a side sail. Its centre provides a landing point for a Kitelet.

items.name: Seed-cup perch B
items.description: A longer, narrower cup turns upward more steeply. A tall side sail and small lower leaf vary the silhouette.

items.name: Seed-cup perch C
items.description: A wider, shorter cup twists across its stem, accompanied by offset side leaves. Five perch instances draw from these three forms.

items.name: Gathered dry stems
items.description: Loose tan twigs lie low in sheltered sand pockets. A Sand Stitcher's carried stem appears in the pile during its placement sequence.

sections.title: Muse and the neighbours
sections.intro: The plush residents share the same character family but have distinct coats and identities. They remain near the settlement on clear walking routes.

items.name: Muse
items.description: The cream-coloured host walks, rests, cooks and naps around the home. Its presence and working state can follow the connected garden source.

items.name: Pip - Sail gardener
items.description: A pale peach neighbour with a gentle walking and resting routine in the clearing. Pip can greet the visitor, be petted and be followed.

items.name: Juniper - Wind listener
items.description: A pale mint neighbour who follows a separate safe lane near the shelter, pausing and responding to the visitor.

items.name: Marlo - Cloud watcher
items.description: A pale blue neighbour living on the other side of the clearing. Marlo shares the residents' greetings, petting and camera-follow interactions.

sections.title: Sky, cloud and light
sections.intro: The atmosphere balances a pale yellow sky with quiet white cloud shapes. The ground view and orbit view use complementary cloud layers.

items.name: Pale butter sky
items.description: A soft yellow gradient brightens toward the horizon, with a subtle sun glow and warm haze behind the landscape.

items.name: Painted sky wisps
items.description: Long ivory shapes drift across the background. Their finite tapered ends and uneven shoulders keep the sky from reading as a set of uniform stripes.

items.name: Planet-wrapping cirrus
items.description: Eighteen soft white ribbons with a faint yellow tint curl around the planet. They retain their tapered shapes and gradually disappear as the camera approaches the ground.

items.name: Matte light and distance haze
items.description: Late-morning light, soft toon bands and restrained paper grain unite the materials. Distant forms recede into a pale blue-grey haze.

sections.title: Saved finds and planted beds
sections.intro: Saved finds take on native Cobalt forms. They are garden records represented by small specimens and companion planting, separate from the ambient colonies.

items.name: Coral find specimen
items.description: A compact rounded fan of branching coral marks a saved find, with its own scale, lean and orientation.

items.name: Ivory sail find specimen
items.description: A small branched stem carries two asymmetric ivory sails, echoing the taller plants of the windfields.

items.name: Cobalt fragment specimen
items.description: A compact angular stone with an uneven crown represents a saved find in the stone family.

items.name: Coral root bed
items.description: Low coral fans cluster around a central specimen, leaving its middle clear and readable.

items.name: Ivory seed-sail bed
items.description: Small ivory sails form companion planting around a saved specimen.

items.name: Young coral root bed
items.description: A second coral bed variant repeats the rounded branching habit at the small garden scale.

items.name: Young seed-sail bed
items.description: A second seed-sail bed variant keeps the same native leaf language in the planted garden records.

items.name: Distant find markers and pins
items.description: Saved specimens transition to small glowing markers high above the ground. Optional pins identify liked finds and Muse's location.

sections.title: Small signs of life
sections.intro: These accents appear during particular activities and interactions, so a frozen landscape view may not show them.

items.name: Petting hearts
items.description: Small hearts rise around a Muse character while it responds to sustained petting.

items.name: Humming notes
items.description: Musical-note motes accompany a quiet humming moment, including Muse's bench routine.

items.name: Nap bubble and sleep marks
items.description: A little bubble and floating sleep marks accompany a resting character's nap.

items.name: Cooking steam
items.description: Soft puffs rise from the porch pot while Muse cooks and stirs.

inactive.name: Conventional meadow grass and flowers
inactive.reason: Inherited systems remain in the code, but Cobalt disables their near-field drawing. The visible native flora is authored separately.

inactive.name: Generic birds and butterflies
inactive.reason: Their inherited meshes are explicitly hidden. Sailbacks, Kitelets and Sand Stitchers are the active ambient fauna.

inactive.name: Water, lakes, ponds, culverts and lily pads
inactive.reason: Compatibility data and controls remain, but the current terrain is entirely dry. The former pier is a stone lookout.

inactive.name: Puffy cloud layer
inactive.reason: Its default coverage is zero. The current visible cloud design uses painted sky wisps and physical cirrus ribbons; shadow infrastructure is retained.

inactive.name: Fishing and watering accessories
inactive.reason: The rod, float, fish and watering can belong to inherited animation assets. Fishing and watering have zero activity weight in Cobalt's local routine.

inactive.name: Roof chimney, snow and generic falling petals
inactive.reason: These are retained constants, palette data or unused scene systems, not current Cobalt environment features. The small porch stove pipe is active.
